4. The plaintiff-opposite Party filed a counter affidavit and resisted this application for rejection of the plaint. The plaintiff stated that he tried to get the agreement registered before the concerned Sub-Registrar but the Sub-Registrar refused to register the agreement for which, he was compelled to institute the suit within the period of limitation. The learned Joint District Judge considered the point agitated by the petitioner and was of the view that this point being a disputed fact would be decided on evidence at the preemptory hearing of the suit. 

 5. Section 17A, 17B, 22A, 52A and 78A were added by way of amendment of the Registration Act by Act XXV of 2004. The said amendment was effective on and from 1st July, 2005. Sections 17A, 17B are relevant for our consideration. Section 17A provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Registration Act, a contract for sale of any immovable property shall be writing executed by the parties thereto and registered and that the said contract shall be presented for registration within 30 days from the date of execution of the contract. In Section 17B there are two clauses. Clause (a) provides that where a con-tract for sale of immovable property is executed but not registered prior to coming into force of section 17A, the parties to the contract shall, within six months from the date of coming into force of that section—present the contract for sale itself for registration. Cause (b) provides that either of the parties, if aggrieved for non-compliance of the provisions mentioned in Clause (a), shall, notwithstanding anything contained to the contrary in any law for the time being in force as to the Law of Limitation, institute a suit for specific performance or recession of the contract within six months next after the expiry of the period mentioned in Clause (a).
